paths.description: Cross-route checks covering shared shell, security, privacy, performance, accessibility, resilience, internationalisation, sustainability, agent readiness, and memory.
Homepage catalog, trending and latest-content archetype; tested desktop, 360px mobile, light preference, reduced motion, keyboard focus, raw HTML and performance/network conditions.
Representative title detail and chapter-list archetype, including metadata, Start reading action and multilingual alternate titles.
Primary browse/detail-to-reader outcome represented by chapter 115, including desktop/mobile page rendering, progress and chapter controls.
Fabricated route used to test HTTP and route-recovery behaviour.

findings.summary: A transparent full-viewport link intercepts the entire experience
findings.evidence: DOM and elementFromPoint probes on the home and reader routes found an unnamed fixed <a target="_blank" href="#"> at z-index 9,999,999 covering 100% of the viewport. It blocks the visible controls and disguises the click target.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the injected full-page anchor, identify and remove the script or third party that creates it, and use explicit, labelled controls only.

findings.summary: The fixed dark palette ignores the user’s color-scheme preference
findings.evidence: Under emulated prefers-color-scheme: light the page remained rgb(14, 19, 27); color-scheme was normal and the loaded CSS contained no prefers-color-scheme rule.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven light and dark tokens using prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: Low-contrast text and controls fail WCAG AA
findings.evidence: axe found 49 serious color-contrast failures and Lighthouse found 44 affected nodes, including active tabs, metadata, buttons and card timestamps. No prefers-contrast or forced-colors CSS was found.
findings.suggestedFix: Raise token contrast to WCAG AA and add forced-colors/prefers-contrast adaptations for essential text and controls.

findings.summary: Route and state changes have no View Transition treatment
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found zero view-transition declarations and the document reported no active animations or view transition names.
findings.suggestedFix: Use same-document View Transitions for card-to-detail and detail-to-reader changes, while respecting reduced motion.

findings.summary: Menus and transient controls do not use resilient anchored positioning
findings.evidence: The loaded CSS contained zero anchor-name, position-anchor or position-try declarations despite multiple menu-like buttons with aria-haspopup.
findings.suggestedFix: Use popover plus CSS anchor positioning and position-try fallbacks for menus and tooltips.

findings.summary: Custom overlay patterns replace semantic dismissible primitives
findings.evidence: Rendered DOM contains many menu controls but no evidence of dialog/popover primitives, while an ad-hoc fixed anchor is used as a page-wide overlay.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace ad-hoc overlays with popover/dialog and declarative light-dismiss; remove the page-wide anchor.

findings.summary: Components rely on viewport styling rather than container responsiveness
findings.evidence: The complete loaded stylesheet contained zero @container rules even though cards, toolbars and reader controls are reused in materially different widths.
findings.suggestedFix: Define component containers and use size/content queries for reusable cards and toolbars.

findings.summary: Zoom is disabled and at least one target is too short
findings.evidence: The homepage viewport sets maximum-scale=1,user-scalable=no; Lighthouse marks this critical and the interaction probe found an 18px-high sync link. Focus styling itself was visible.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove scaling restrictions and ensure interactive targets meet accessible target-size guidance without relying on hover.

findings.summary: The primary browse-to-read flow is visually present but click-blocked
findings.evidence: The reader loaded 62 pages and responsive controls, but elementFromPoint at the viewport center returns the transparent z-index 9,999,999 anchor rather than the reader; the same blocker exists on browse and detail pages.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the click-capturing overlay and add an end-to-end browse, open title, start reading regression test.

findings.summary: Unknown routes return the homepage with HTTP 200 instead of a recovery state
findings.evidence: A fabricated path returned HTTP 200 and rendered the normal homepage with no not-found message, search recovery, or route correction.
findings.suggestedFix: Return a real 404 and a useful recovery page with search, Home, and previous-page actions.

findings.summary: Mobile LCP is well outside the good threshold
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 5.7s and FCP 3.2s (performance 0.72), although TBT was only 10ms and CLS 0.042. The local trace corroborated a lighter warm-path LCP of 1.20s.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the actual LCP image, reduce render-blocking resources, and validate cold mobile LCP below 2.5s.

findings.summary: Image and critical-resource delivery is inefficient
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 60 requests and 1,754,011 transferred bytes; Lighthouse estimated 887 KiB image savings, found render-blocking requests and poor LCP discovery, while 62/62 homepage images lacked dimensions.
findings.suggestedFix: Use responsive modern images with explicit dimensions, prioritise the LCP image, and trim render-blocking/font dependency chains.

findings.summary: The initial route ships avoidable unused code
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 112 KiB unused JavaScript and 16 KiB unused CSS on the homepage.
findings.suggestedFix: Route-split the bundle and conditionally load reader, account and sharing code only where needed.

findings.summary: An interactive full-page link has no accessible name
findings.evidence: axe and Lighthouse both report one serious unnamed link; it is the full-viewport target=_blank overlay. The page also had one input without a programmatic label.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the overlay link and give every remaining input/link a visible or programmatic accessible name.

findings.summary: Homepage landmarks and heading structure are invalid
findings.evidence: axe found nested/duplicate main landmarks; the DOM probe found two MAIN elements and no h1 on the homepage. Visible keyboard focus did pass.
findings.suggestedFix: Use one top-level main landmark and a logical h1-first heading hierarchy per route.

findings.summary: The viewport prevents user zoom
findings.evidence: The homepage meta viewport uses maximum-scale=1,user-scalable=no; both axe and Lighthouse classify this as a failure.
findings.suggestedFix: Use width=device-width, initial-scale=1 and do not restrict zoom.

findings.summary: Deprecated APIs and unsized assets remain
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported three deprecated API warnings and unsized images; the image primitive found all 62 homepage images lacked width/height attributes. Doctype and charset were valid.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove deprecated API use and add intrinsic width/height or aspect-ratio to all images.

findings.summary: Crawler-facing navigation is effectively absent without JavaScript
findings.evidence: Discoverability measured 1% raw/rendered word coverage and a JS shell; direct robots.txt and sitemap.xml requests returned 403, and the only unnamed rendered link is the overlay.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render core listings and links; publish accessible robots.txt and sitemap.xml; remove the unnamed overlay.

findings.summary: Canonical and error indexing signals are unreliable
findings.evidence: No canonical link was present, robots/sitemap returned 403 to a plain client, and a nonexistent URL returned a soft-404 HTTP 200 homepage.
findings.suggestedFix: Add route-specific canonical URLs, serve consistent robots/sitemap responses, and return correct 404 status codes.

findings.summary: Detail pages lack entity metadata and use generic social previews
findings.evidence: The detail DOM had no JSON-LD; its og:title remained “MangaFire - Read Manga Online Free” rather than the visible title “All-Class Awakening: God Slayer”.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit route-specific Open Graph metadata and schema.org JSON-LD for series/title entities.

findings.summary: Core browser security headers and a Secure session cookie are missing
findings.evidence: The page uses HTTPS, but headers found no CSP, HSTS, nosniff, frame defense, Referrer-Policy or Permissions-Policy; the session cookie lacked Secure.
findings.suggestedFix: Mark the session cookie Secure and deploy a restrictive CSP, HSTS, nosniff, frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy.

findings.summary: Tracking/share requests are made without a clear need or disclosure
findings.evidence: The tracker probe saw six third-party origins, including whos.amung.us and count-server.sharethis.com; 51 of 60 HAR requests and 1.72 MB were classified third party.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove nonessential counters, self-host essential assets where practical, and gate analytics on clear purpose and consent.

findings.summary: No defensive browser policies are configured
findings.evidence: Header evidence found no clickjacking defense, CSP/Trusted Types policy, HSTS, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy or nosniff protection.
findings.suggestedFix: Set defense-in-depth headers, starting with CSP frame-ancestors, HSTS, nosniff, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy.

findings.summary: Core content disappears when JavaScript is unavailable
findings.evidence: Raw HTML contained only five content tokens versus 263 rendered tokens; discoverability classified the response as a JS shell with 1% coverage.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render the catalog and title content with real links, then enhance interaction on the client.

findings.summary: The reading app has no manifest, service worker or offline fallback
findings.evidence: The platform probe found neither a manifest nor an active service worker on this app-like reader.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a web app manifest and a service-worker-backed offline/error shell, while caching only lawful, appropriate resources.

findings.summary: Multilingual content is wrapped in an English, physically positioned UI
findings.evidence: The detail page exposes titles in many scripts, but html is fixed lang=en with implicit direction; CSS inspection found 140 physical left/right declarations versus four logical-property uses.
findings.suggestedFix: Use language metadata for multilingual strings, explicit direction where needed, and migrate layout to logical properties.

findings.summary: Image assets are not delivered sustainably
findings.evidence: The image audit found 62 legacy-format images, 30 without srcset, 15 oversized, and no modern-format image; HAR attributed 1.37 MB to images.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate AVIF/WebP variants and responsive srcset/sizes, reserve dimensions, and lazy-load below-fold content.

findings.summary: The homepage performs disproportionate initial work
findings.evidence: The initial view makes 60 requests and transfers 1.75 MB, while Lighthouse identifies unused JS/CSS and hundreds of KiB of avoidable image transfer.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer below-fold cards and nonessential sharing/tracking, and route-split code so initial work serves the first viewport.

findings.summary: Third-party transfer dominates the page budget
findings.evidence: HAR classified 51 requests and 1,724,576 bytes as third party, including external image/CDN, font, counter and sharing origins.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party budget, self-host fonts, remove counters, and defer optional integrations until requested.

findings.summary: Public catalog content is not reliably available to agents
findings.evidence: Discoverability reports a 1% JS-shell response, Lighthouse agentic browsing scored 0.33 with malformed accessibility-tree and llms.txt signals, and no structured entity data was found.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render semantic catalog/title content and structured data first; add safe structured agent capabilities only for actions that benefit users.

taskList.title: Remove the transparent full-page click-capturing anchor and its injector
Deploy secure cookies and browser security headers
Server-render core catalog, title metadata, links, and correct 404 responses
Fix contrast, zoom, landmarks, names, and target sizes
Optimise image/LCP delivery and split unused route code
Add preference-driven theming and contrast adaptations
Modernise component responsiveness, overlays, anchors, and route transitions
Add resilient offline/error handling and reduce third-party tracking
